editorial:
Imagine winning a dream trip to the sunny south of France, only to accidentally cause chaos everywhere you go. That is exactly what happens when the lovable, clumsy Mr. Bean heads to Cannes. Along the way, he accidentally separates a young boy from his father, a famous film director, and feels responsible for fixing the mess. What follows is a silly, warm-hearted road trip filled with misunderstandings, funny faces, and plenty of slapstick moments. The movie has a light, breezy feel that makes it easy to watch with the whole family.

Rowan Atkinson carries the whole film with his amazing physical comedy, and the beautiful French scenery adds a nice touch. The story moves quickly and never drags, though some jokes feel a bit repetitive if you are not already a fan. If you love goofy, old-school humor, this is a great pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Mr. Bean finally reaches the Cannes film festival just as the boy's father's movie is being shown. Bean accidentally ends up on stage and on the big screen, but instead of ruining things, his silly antics win over the crowd. The boy reunites with his father, and Bean gets a happy ending of his own when he shares a sweet moment with Sabine, the actress he met along the way. It is a feel-good finish that ties everything together nicely.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves goofy physical comedy and lighthearted family fun.
